messages.author: 5a7c50cc48efe23c
messages.subject: Creating more informative priors
parts:
Hi there,

I want to follow up on comment re. memory: 

"My guess, is that it is using all the time 
getting the last digits of a very flat posterior right. You'll see this 
easily in the output. Also it will say 'switch to stupid search mode' or 
something, which is also a bad sign if it stays to long there. I guess 
there are model components, like a rw2, that is essentially a linear 
trend, which creates trouble. More informative priors may also help."

I have maxed out memory of a 16 node 128gb w/ 16core HPC machine trying to run a subset of my data. I am getting all the "stupid" and "I'll fix it" warnings in the optimization step.The model is taking approx. 28hrs to run on this system. 

So, the next step is using more informative priors. How do I determine these?

-Erin

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Creating more informative priors
parts:
The closest we get to giving you a default prior to use is found as a comment in
inla.doc("rw1")
under "Current recommended prior".

Let me know if this helps,
Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
